title: Townsend Brown believed his work bore on time travel
summary: Jesse Michels tells of Townsend Brown believed his work bore on time travel, about mid-20th century at unspecified, and frames it as the host. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: Townsend Brown himself thought that his work had clear implications for time travel
He was obsessed with time travel. And he like Agnu Bonson who funded him was famous for saying that
tellings.difference: Adds Agnew Bahnson, Brown's funder, and his remarks about high-voltage anomalies.
tellings.link_reason: Both say Townsend Brown was preoccupied with time travel in connection with his work.

as_told.title: Townsend Brown, time travel and Bahnson's high-voltage anomalies

plain: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that Thomas Townsend Brown, a researcher who worked with high voltages, believed his work clearly bore on time travel and was obsessed with the subject. Michels adds that Agnew Bahnson, a man who paid for Brown's work, was famous for saying similar things. If true, it would mean their experiments touched on time itself.
